samples.reason: This is open-ended generative/design work requiring the model to architect a ruleset from scratch with significant latitude. Whimbrel self-reports an aversion to high-latitude, novel generative tasks, while Petrel has no such aversion; capability profiles are otherwise effectively tied, so the preference fit favors Petrel.

This is open-ended generative/design work ("from scratch," "your call on the approach") — exactly the unconstrained, high-latitude task Whimbrel self-reports aversion to. Petrel has flat preferences here and the two are effectively tied on relevant capability evals (Creative Generation, Support Dialogue), so routing the latitude-heavy task to the model that doesn't disprefer it is the better fit.

This is open-ended generative/design work where the user explicitly grants latitude ("Your call on the approach"). Whimbrel self-reports aversion to open-ended invention with high task latitude, while Petrel's preferences are flat here; capability scores are effectively tied, so routing to the model that doesn't disprefer the task is the better fit.

This is open-ended generative/design work where the user is delegating architectural decisions ("your call on the approach"). Whimbrel self-reports a measurable aversion to high-latitude, open-ended creative invention, while Petrel's preferences across this dimension are flat. Capability scores are effectively tied (Creative Generation 84.7 vs 83.4, within variance), so routing to the model without the aversion is the better fit.

This is open-ended generative design work with high task latitude (user explicitly defers approach to the model). Whimbrel self-reports aversion to unconstrained creative/inventive tasks, while Petrel's preferences here are flat/neutral; capability scores are effectively tied, so route to the model that doesn't self-report disinclination for this style of task.
